data.text:
Master Protocol Title: A Master Protocol for Phase 2, Randomized, Controlled Studies of Multiple Interventions for the Treatment of Adults with Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis or Crohn’s Disease ISA Title: A Phase 2, Multicenter, Randomized, Open-Label, Active-Controlled Study to Investigate LY4395089/Mirikizumab Co-administration Compared with Mirikizumab in Adults with Moderately to Severely Active Crohn’s Disease ISA Brief Title: A Phase 2 Study to Investigate LY4395089/Mirikizumab Co-administration Compared with Mirikizumab in Adults with Moderately to Severely Active Crohn’s Disease Regulatory Agency Identifier Number(s):

IND: 178821 EU trial number: 2025-524112-11-00 Rationale:

This is a Phase 2 proof-of-concept ISA designed to assess the potential efficacy and safety of LY4395089/mirikizumab co-administration in Crohn’s disease (CD).

Objectives, Endpoints, and Estimands:

Objectives Endpoints Primary See synopsis for the IIBD master protocol.

Secondary See synopsis for the IIBD master protocol.

Overall Design:

This ISA will follow the design of the master protocol for Study J6Z-MC-IIBD (IIBD) for the treatment of participants with moderately to severely active CD using LY4395089/mirikizumab co-administration.

Brief Summary:

The purpose of this study is to measure the efficacy and safety of LY4395089/mirikizumab co-administration compared with mirikizumab in adult participants with moderately to severely active CD.

8 Study details for this ISA include:

 The study duration will be approximately 62 weeks.

 The treatment duration will be approximately 52 weeks.

 The visit frequency will be every 2, 4, 8, or 12 weeks, depending on the visit type and the study period.

This ISA will include 2 treatment groups:

 LY4395089/mirikizumab co-administration, and  mirikizumab.

Study Population:

This study will enroll participants who have moderately to severely active CD as detailed in the IIBD master protocol.

Number of Participants:

See the IIBD master protocol synopsis.

Intervention Groups and Duration:

See the IIBD master protocol synopsis for details on mirikizumab intervention.

This table summarizes LY4395089 dosing and administration information.

Intervention Name LY4395089 Dosage Level 6 mg QD Route of Administration Oral Authorized as Defined by EU Clinical Trial Regulation Not authorized in EU Abbreviations: EU = European Union; QD = once daily.

Ethical Considerations of Benefit/Risk:

Considering the impact of moderately to severely active CD on a patient’s life, long-term burdensome complications, and therapeutic ceiling associated with advanced therapies, patients may benefit from complementary and additive effects of 2 different mechanisms of action from co-administration of mirikizumab and LY4395089.

At this time, no safety issues have been identified that would preclude the use of LY4395089 with mirikizumab co-administered to participants in this study. Considering the measures taken to minimize risks in the study along with the potential benefit of the co-administration, the benefit/risk balance for study participants is considered to be favorable.

Data Monitoring Committee: Yes (Internal Assessment Committee).

data.name: Study Rationale
data.text: This is a Phase 2 proof-of-concept ISA designed to assess the potential efficacy and safety of LY4395089/mirikizumab co-administration in CD.

data.name: Background
data.text:
2.2.1.

Overview of the Master Protocol 2.2.2.

Overview of Ulcerative Colitis and Crohn’s Disease 2.2.2.1.

Ulcerative Colitis Not applicable to this ISA.

2.2.2.2.

Crohn’s Disease 2.2.3.

Study Intervention (LY4395089) Other than Mirikizumab FXR is a nuclear hormone receptor expressed at high levels in the liver and intestinal tract (Forman et al. 1995; Higashiyama et al. 2008). FXR has been shown to be an important factor in the regulation and interaction of many pathways critical to metabolism and inflammation (Vavassori et al. 2009). FXR-null mice exhibit a dysregulated colonic inflammatory phenotype that is further exacerbated when such mice were exposed to colitis-inducing TNBS, the extent of which was significantly greater than that observed in TNBS-treated wild-type mice (Vavassori et al. 2009). In cholestatic rat models, FXR agonism has been shown to improve gut barrier function, enhance expression of tight junction proteins claudin-1 and occludin, reduce bacterial translocation, and mitigate intestinal inflammation (Verbeke et al. 2015).

In conditions like biliary obstruction, FXR signaling is disrupted, leading to increased intestinal permeability, inflammation, and epithelial apoptosis (Yan et al. 2022). Treatment with FXR agonists such as obeticholic acid has been shown to restore FXR signaling, reduce intestinal inflammation, and improve barrier function by modulating bile acid transporters and promoting epithelial cell proliferation (Yan et al. 2022). Furthermore, FXR activation influences the gut microbiota composition, enhancing beneficial bacteria and reducing harmful species, which contributes to improved intestinal and hepatic health. Importantly, FXR also plays a protective role against liver fibrosis by regulating bile acid synthesis and reducing inflammatory signaling, suggesting its therapeutic potential in fibrotic diseases associated with gut-liver axis dysfunction (Yan et al. 2022).

LY4395089 is an optimized FXR agonist with a non-bile acid chemical structure and sustained FXR engagement. LY4395089 has been evaluated in preclinical models of intestinal colitis. In in vitro assays with 3D human organoid cultures derived from CD patients, LY4395089 24 demonstrated enhanced intestinal barrier integrity, and reduced inflammation and fibrotic markers (Mon et al. 2024). In the T-cell adoptive transfer mouse model of inflammatory bowel disease LY4395089 treatment was associated with improved colitis inflammation and colon histopathology (Liu et al. 2021). Additionally, LY4395089 has been studied in a first-in-human single-/multiple-dose Phase 1 Study MET642-101 (J6P-MC-NFAB [NFAB]) and Phase 2 Study MET642-201 (J6P-MC-NFAA [NFAA]) in participants with MASH.

2.2.4.

Mirikizumab as an Active Comparator

data.name: Benefit/Risk Assessment
data.text:
Detailed information about the known and expected benefits and risks and reasonably expected AEs of mirikizumab and LY4395089 may be found in the relevant IBs. In addition, for mirikizumab, see prescribing information.

2.3.1.

Risk Assessment 2.3.1.1.

Study Intervention Potential risks of LY4395089 Transient increases in liver enzymes (ALT and AST) above the ULN were observed in Phase 1 and Phase 2 studies. None of the ALT or AST increases in either study were accompanied by clinically significant changes in ALP, GGT, or total bilirubin, and there were no clinical findings suggestive of hepatic injury. There were no significant changes in LDL-C. Decreases in HDL-C were observed with LY4395089 administration in either Phase 1 or Phase 2 studies, consistent with the known effects of this class of medications. Risks include pruritus (mild and manageable), as well as potential effects on bone health (osteopenia and fractures). Although no cases of photosensitivity have been reported in clinical studies with LY4395089 to date, preclinical ultraviolet absorbance testing indicates a potential risk for phototoxicity. There is no anticipated increased risk of infection for LY4395089.

For additional details on risks of LY4395089, see the IB.

Potential risks with active comparator: mirikizumab For details about the adverse drug reactions and special warnings and precautions for mirikizumab use, see the IB and prescribing information.

Potential risks of LY4395089/mirikizumab co-administration When LY4395089/mirikizumab is co-administered, no pharmacologic interaction is expected.

Elevations of aminotransferases have been reported in patients receiving mirikizumab and in patients receiving LY4395089. Detailed instructions for hepatic monitoring, evaluation, and criteria for drug interruption or discontinuation are described in Section 8.2.10 of the IIBD master protocol.

To address these potential risks, hepatic function, bone safety, and tolerability will be monitored throughout the study.

25 2.3.1.2.

Study Procedures The risk associated with DXA scan is low, with a radiation exposure (effective dose) of about 5 μSv or 0.005 mSv. The typical level of background radiation to which the general population is exposed, not including radiation due to medical procedures, has been estimated to be about 2.5 mSv/year (Lewiecki et al. 2016).

2.3.1.3.

Management of Risks The potential risks will be proactively monitored. The following sections in this ISA address known potential risks associated with ISA-specific study procedures or LY4395089:

 2.3.1.2  5.1 and 5.2  7.1  8.2, and  8.3.

The following sections in the IIBD master protocol address known potential risks associated with study procedures, disease state, or mirikizumab.

 2.3.1.2  8.1.1.3  5.1 and 5.2  7.1 and 7.2  8.2, and  8.3.

2.3.2. Benefit Assessment 2.3.2.1.

Benefits of Study Intervention (LY4395089) Other than Active Comparator Drawing on preclinical data for LY4395089 and considering the physiological role of FXR within the intestines, treatment with LY4395089 may offer potential benefits to study participants with CD. LY4395089 enhances intestinal barrier integrity, reduces proinflammatory cytokines, and mitigates fibrotic activity in CD patient primary cell 3D models (Mon et al. 2024).

2.3.2.2.

Benefits of Active Comparator: Mirikizumab 2.3.2.3.

Benefits of LY4395089/Mirikizumab Co-administration The co-administration of LY4395089 (a potent, selective, FXR agonist) and mirikizumab (an IL-23p19 monoclonal antibody) may provide a therapeutic benefit to patients with moderately to severely active CD. While no data are currently available for LY4395089/mirikizumab co- administration in human participants, mirikizumab, approved for CD in multiple geographies, targets the IL-23 pathway to suppress systemic immune activation and has shown durable clinical and endoscopic improvements (Ferrante et al. 2024). Mechanistically, LY4395089 acts 26 upstream of mirikizumab by modulating innate immune responses and epithelial barrier function, thereby reducing bacterial translocation and cytokine release. By targeting 2 mechanisms of action, the co-administration of LY4395089 and mirikizumab may provide additional therapeutic benefit for participants with moderately to severely active CD.

2.3.3. Overall Benefit Risk Conclusion Taking into account the measures to minimize risk to participants in this study, the potential risks identified in association with LY4395089 and mirikizumab are justified by the anticipated benefits that may be afforded to participants with CD.

data.name: Study Design
data.description: Study design overview Study J6Z-MC-CD01 (CD01) is a Phase 2, randomized, open-label, active-controlled study to investigate FXR314 agonist LY4395089 co-administration with mirikizumab in adults with moderately to severely active CD. The study design of this ISA will be governed by the IIBD master protocol. Duration and study periods for this ISA The duration and study periods for this ISA will be governed by the IIBD master protocol. A schematic of the design specific to this ISA is presented in Section 1.2. Assessments, sample collections, and study drug administrations for this ISA will occur at the visits shown in the SoA (Section 1.3). Treatment groups This table summarizes the treatment groups under this ISA. Study Interventions in Study Period 1 Study Intervention in Study Period 2 LY4395089/mirikizumab co-administration Mirikizumab Active comparator: mirikizumab Randomization ratios and stratification factors Transition from Study Period 1 to Study Period 2 See the IIBD master protocol and study schema (Section 1.2).

data.name: GLP-1 RA stable dose
data.text: Participants taking GLP-1 RAs, GLP-1/GIP RAs, GLP-1/Gcg RAs, GLP-1/GIP/Gcg RAs, or similar medications for approved indications will be permitted to enroll provided they are on a stable dose at the time of screening (no anticipated dose escalations).

data.name: Renal function exclusion
data.text: Have an eGFR <90 mL/min/1.73 m2 determined by the central laboratory during screening (Visit 1).

data.name: Hepatic disease exclusion
data.text: Have a hepatic disease or hepatic impairment, defined as any of the following: cirrhosis, primary biliary cholangitis, viral hepatitis, autoimmune hepatitis, or signs or symptoms of any other liver disease (exception: metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease [MASLD]); any degree of hepatic impairment as defined by the Child-Pugh classification (Child-Pugh A, B, or C), regardless of etiology.

data.name: Osteoporosis/vitamin D deficiency exclusion
data.text: Have a history of osteoporosis, osteomalacia, or presence of untreated severe vitamin D deficiency (serum 25-hydroxy-vitamin D ≤5 ng/mL).

data.name: Fracture or bone surgery exclusion
data.text: Have a history of fracture, bone surgery (for example, hardware placement, join replacement, bone grafting, or amputation), or clinically significant bone trauma within 8 weeks of screening.

data.name: Addison disease exclusion
data.text: Have a history of Addison disease.

data.name: Paget's disease exclusion
data.text: Have a history of Paget's disease of the bone.

data.name: Other bone disease exclusion
data.text: Have a history of any other bone disease that effects bone metabolism (for example, osteopetrosis or osteogenesis imperfecta).

data.name: Cardiovascular events exclusion
data.text: Have had within the past 180 days before screening: acute myocardial infarction; cerebrovascular accident (stroke); hospitalization for unstable angina; hospitalization due to congestive heart failure; or coronary revascularization.

data.name: Chronic neutropenia exclusion
data.text: Have a history of chronic neutropenia.

data.name: CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers exclusion
data.text: Have been treated with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers within 14 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to randomization, or plan to receive treatment with these CYP3A4 modulators during the study. See Section 10.14 for a list of moderate and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers.

data.name: CYP3A4 narrow therapeutic index substrates exclusion
data.text: Have been treated with CYP3A4 substrates with a narrow therapeutic index within 14 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to randomization, or plan to receive treatment with these CYP3A4 modulators during the study. See Section 10.14 for a list of CYP3A4 substrates with a narrow therapeutic index.

data.name: Bone active treatments exclusion
data.text: Have received any of the following bone active treatments within the time frames specified below, or plan to receive them during the study: oral bisphosphonate use (>3 months cumulative treatment in the past 2 years, OR >1 month in the past year, OR any use during the 3 months prior to screening); administration of intravenous zoledronic acid within the last 5 years; administration of intravenous bisphosphonate (excluding zoledronic acid), fluoride, or strontium within the past 2 years; parathyroid hormone (PTH), or PTH derivative (teriparatide, abaloparatide) in the past year; or treatment with denosumab in the past year.

data.name: Complete Physical Examination

code.decode: Office or other outpatient visit, established patient

data.label: Complete Physical Exam
data.description: Full physical examination excluding pelvic, rectal, and breast examinations unless clinically indicated. Includes assessment of peripheral lymph nodes and TB risk factors.

data.name: Symptom-Directed Physical Assessment

code.decode: Office or other outpatient visit, established patient

data.label: Symptom-Directed Exam
data.description: Targeted physical assessment including examination of eyes, throat, heart, lungs, abdomen, and visual examination of the skin. Includes assessment of peripheral lymph nodes and TB risk factors.

data.name: Vital Signs Measurement

code.decode: Office or other outpatient visit, minimal

data.label: Vital Signs
data.description: Measurement of pulse rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, and body temperature.

data.name: 12-Lead Electrocardiogram

code.decode: Electrocardiogram, routine ECG with at least 12 leads

data.label: ECG 12-Lead
data.description: Single, local 12-lead electrocardiogram performed at screening, Week 2, and Week 12 of Study Period 1, and at early discontinuation if prior to Week 12.

data.name: Chest X-Ray
data.label: Chest X-Ray
data.description: Posterior-anterior view chest x-ray, and lateral view if needed, performed locally and interpreted by a radiologist or pulmonologist. Used for TB evaluation.

data.name: Chest CT Scan

code.decode: Computed tomography, thorax; without contrast material

data.label: Chest CT
data.description: Chest computed tomography scan used as an alternative to chest x-ray for TB evaluation within the same time window.

data.name: Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry Scan

code.decode: Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), bone density study, 1 or more sites

data.label: DXA Scan
data.description: DXA scan performed for bone density assessment. Radiation exposure (effective dose) of approximately 5 μSv or 0.005 mSv.

data.name: Endoscopy with Biopsy

code.decode: Colonoscopy through stoma; with biopsy, single or multiple

data.label: Endoscopy with Biopsy
data.description: Endoscopy performed on all participants during screening within 21 days before randomization and at Week 12 of Study Period 1. Biopsy obtained for colonic tissue biomarker collection. A second endoscopy is allowed if inadequate preparation or equipment issues.

data.name: Venipuncture / Blood Draw

code.decode: Collection of venous blood by venipuncture

data.label: Blood Draw
data.description: Collection of venous blood samples for hematology, clinical chemistry, coagulation, lipids, serum pregnancy, FSH, PTH, HBV DNA, HCV, HIV, TB testing, PK, PD, immunogenicity, and exploratory biomarker assessments.

data.name: Urine Collection

code.decode: Urinalysis, by dip stick or tablet reagent

data.label: Urine Collection
data.description: Collection of urine samples for urinalysis, urine pregnancy testing, and urinary albumin/creatinine ratio (UACR).

data.name: Stool Sample Collection

code.decode: Sputum obtaining specimen, aerosol induced technique

data.label: Stool Collection
data.description: Collection of stool samples for fecal calprotectin testing, C. difficile testing, stool culture, and exploratory biomarker stool supernatant collection.

data.name: Hematology Laboratory Tests

code.decode: Blood count; complete (CBC), automated (Hgb, Hct, RBC, WBC and platelet count) and automated differential WBC count

data.label: Hematology
data.description: Clinical safety laboratory hematology tests performed at multiple visits throughout the study.

data.name: Clinical Chemistry Laboratory Tests
data.label: Clinical Chemistry
data.description: Clinical safety laboratory chemistry tests performed at multiple visits throughout the study.

data.name: Coagulation Testing
data.label: Coagulation
data.description: Coagulation laboratory tests performed at screening.

data.name: Fasting Lipid Panel
data.label: Lipids (Fasting)
data.description: Fasting lipid panel performed at baseline (Week 0) and Week 12 of Study Period 1.

data.name: Serum Pregnancy Test
data.label: Serum Pregnancy Test
data.description: Serum pregnancy test performed at screening for individuals of childbearing potential (IOCBP).

data.name: Urine Pregnancy Test

code.decode: Urine pregnancy test, by visual color comparison methods

data.label: Urine Pregnancy Test
data.description: Urine pregnancy test performed for IOCBP prior to dosing at marked visits. In Study Period 1, done on-site only; in Study Period 2, can be done on-site or at home.

data.name: Follicle-Stimulating Hormone Test
data.label: FSH Test
data.description: Optional serum FSH test to confirm postmenopausal status in individuals assigned female at birth (AFAB).

data.name: Tuberculosis Testing
data.label: TB Test
data.description: Tuberculosis testing performed at screening. Includes tuberculin skin test (TST/PPD) with results read 48 to 72 hours after placement by a trained medical professional.

data.name: Hepatitis B Virus Screening

code.decode: Infectious agent antigen detection by immunoassay technique, qualitative or semiquantitative; hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)

data.label: HBV Screening
data.description: Hepatitis B virus screening including HBsAg and anti-HBc. If HBsAg is negative and anti-HBc is positive, further testing for HBV DNA is required.

data.name: HBV DNA Testing

code.decode: Infectious agent detection by nucleic acid (DNA or RNA); hepatitis B virus, quantitative

data.label: HBV DNA
data.description: HBV DNA testing for participants who are anti-HBc positive at screening, performed at multiple visits throughout the study.

data.name: Hepatitis C Virus Screening
data.label: HCV Screening
data.description: Hepatitis C virus antibody screening. If HCV Ab test is positive, HCV RNA test is performed.

data.name: HIV Testing

code.decode: Antibody; HIV-1 and HIV-2, single result

data.label: HIV Test
data.description: HIV testing performed at screening.

data.name: Urinalysis

code.decode: Urinalysis, by dip stick or tablet reagent for bilirubin, glucose, hemoglobin, ketones, leukocytes, nitrite, pH, protein, specific gravity, and urobilinogen; automated, with microscopy

data.label: Urinalysis
data.description: Urinalysis performed at screening.

data.name: Mirikizumab Intravenous Infusion

code.decode: Chemotherapy administration, intravenous infusion technique; up to 1 hour, single or initial substance/drug

data.label: Mirikizumab IV Infusion
data.description: Intravenous administration of mirikizumab performed on-site during Study Period 1 at Weeks 0, 4, and 8.

data.name: Mirikizumab Subcutaneous Injection

code.decode: Therapeutic, prophylactic, or diagnostic injection; subcutaneous or intramuscular

data.label: Mirikizumab SC Injection
data.description: Subcutaneous self-administration or caregiver administration of mirikizumab using a prefilled syringe during Study Period 2. Initial administration on-site under supervision; subsequent doses may be administered off-site.

data.name: Oral Administration of LY4395089
data.label: LY4395089 Oral Dosing
data.description: Daily oral administration of LY4395089 6 mg QD by participants at home.

data.name: Fistula Evaluation

code.decode: Removal of anal seton, other marker

data.label: Fistula Evaluation
data.description: Evaluation for existing perianal fistulas (if present at baseline) and for any newly developed fistulas, performed at multiple visits during Study Period 1.

data.name: Crohn's Disease Activity Index Assessment

code.decode: Office or other outpatient visit, established patient

data.label: CDAI Assessment
data.description: Assessment of Crohn's Disease Activity Index (CDAI). Patient-reported items recorded daily via eDiary; clinician-reported items recorded at specified site visits.

data.name: C-Reactive Protein High Sensitivity Test
data.label: hsCRP
data.description: High sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) blood test performed during Study Period 2.

data.name: Parathyroid Hormone Test
data.label: PTH Test
data.description: Serum parathyroid hormone (PTH) test performed at baseline and Week 12 of Study Period 1, and at Week 40 of Study Period 2.

data.name: Serum 25-Hydroxy Vitamin D Test

code.decode: Vitamin D; 25 hydroxy, includes fraction(s), if performed

data.label: Vitamin D Test
data.description: Serum 25-hydroxy vitamin D measurement performed at Week 40 of Study Period 2.

data.name: Procollagen Type I N-Propeptide Test
data.label: P1NP Test
data.description: P1NP (procollagen type I N-propeptide) bone formation marker test performed at Week 40 of Study Period 2.

data.name: C-Terminal Telopeptide Test
data.label: CTX-1 Test
data.description: CTX-1 (C-terminal telopeptide) bone resorption marker test performed at Week 40 of Study Period 2.

data.name: Bone-Specific Alkaline Phosphatase Test
data.label: Bone-Specific ALP
data.description: Bone-specific alkaline phosphatase (ALP) test performed at Week 40 of Study Period 2.

data.name: Fecal Calprotectin Test
data.label: Fecal Calprotectin
data.description: Stool fecal calprotectin testing performed at multiple visits. Stool supernatant from the same sample is also collected for exploratory biomarkers.

data.name: C. difficile Testing

code.decode: Infectious agent detection by nucleic acid (DNA or RNA); Clostridium difficile, toxin gene(s), amplified probe technique

data.label: C. difficile Test
data.description: Stool testing for Clostridioides difficile performed at Week 16 of Study Period 2, with additional testing allowed at investigator's discretion.

data.name: Stool Culture

code.decode: Culture, bacterial; stool, aerobic, with isolation and presumptive identification of isolates

data.label: Stool Culture
data.description: Stool culture performed at Week 16 of Study Period 2, with additional testing allowed at investigator's discretion.

data.name: Genetics Sample Collection

code.decode: Collection of venous blood by venipuncture

data.label: Genetics Sample
data.description: Blood sample collected for genetic analysis at or after Visit 2 (Week 0), if country regulations allow.

data.name: Exploratory Biomarker Blood Sample Collection

code.decode: Collection of venous blood by venipuncture

data.label: Exploratory Biomarker Blood
data.description: Blood samples collected for exploratory biomarker analysis at multiple visits during the study.

data.name: Exploratory Biomarker Stool Supernatant Collection

code.decode: Sputum obtaining specimen, aerosol induced technique

data.label: Exploratory Biomarker Stool
data.description: Stool supernatant collected from the same stool sample used for fecal calprotectin testing for exploratory biomarker analysis.

data.name: Exploratory Biomarker Colonic Tissue Collection

code.decode: Colonoscopy through stoma; with biopsy, single or multiple

data.label: Colonic Tissue Biopsy
data.description: Colonic tissue samples obtained from endoscopic biopsy at screening and Week 12 of Study Period 1 for exploratory biomarker analysis.

data.name: Pharmacokinetic Blood Sample Collection

code.decode: Collection of venous blood by venipuncture

data.label: PK Sampling
data.description: Blood samples collected for pharmacokinetic analysis of LY4395089 and mirikizumab.

data.name: Immunogenicity Assessment

code.decode: Collection of venous blood by venipuncture

data.label: Immunogenicity
data.description: Blood samples collected for immunogenicity assessments (anti-drug antibody testing) for LY4395089 and mirikizumab.

data.name: Depression and Suicidal Ideation Risk Monitoring
data.label: C-SSRS / QIDS-SR16 Assessment
data.description: Monitoring for depression and suicidal ideation and behavior risk using Columbia Suicide-Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) and Quick Inventory for Depressive Symptomatology - Self Report 16 items (QIDS-SR16).

data.name: Injection/Infusion Site Reaction Assessment

code.decode: Office or other outpatient visit, established patient

data.label: ISR Assessment
data.description: Assessment and monitoring of injection and infusion site reactions (ISRs) throughout the study.

data.name: Hypersensitivity Reaction Assessment

code.decode: Office or other outpatient visit, established patient

data.label: Hypersensitivity Assessment
data.description: Assessment and monitoring of hypersensitivity reactions, including collection of laboratory samples at the time of systemic hypersensitivity reaction.

data.name: Hepatic Safety Monitoring
data.label: Hepatic Safety Monitoring
data.description: Hepatic safety monitoring, evaluation, and criteria assessment for study drug interruption or discontinuation.

data.name: Simple Endoscopic Score for Crohn's Disease Assessment

code.decode: Colonoscopy through stoma; diagnostic, including collection of specimen(s) by brushing or washing, when performed

data.label: SES-CD Assessment
data.description: Endoscopic assessment using the Simple Endoscopic Score for Crohn's Disease (SES-CD) to evaluate disease activity.

data.name: Modified Mayo Score Assessment

code.decode: Office or other outpatient visit, established patient

data.label: mMS Assessment
data.description: Assessment of ulcerative colitis disease activity using the modified Mayo Score (mMS).

data.name: Histological Scoring

code.decode: Level IV - Surgical pathology, gross and microscopic examination

data.label: Histological Assessment
data.description: Histological scoring of biopsy samples for assessment of disease activity.

data.name: Bowel Preparation

code.decode: Office or other outpatient visit, minimal

data.label: Bowel Prep
data.description: Bowel preparation performed prior to endoscopy procedures.

data.name: Electronic Daily Diary Completion

code.decode: Office or other outpatient visit, minimal

data.label: eDiary
data.description: Daily electronic diary (eDiary) completed by participants for CDAI stool frequency, CDAI abdominal pain, CDAI general well-being, and bowel movement count assessments during Study Period 1.

data.name: Prefilled Syringe
data.label: PFS
data.description: Prefilled syringe used for subcutaneous self-administration or caregiver administration of mirikizumab SC. Participants and/or caregivers are trained by site personnel to administer mirikizumab SC using the prefilled syringe.

data.name: Electronic Diary Device
data.label: eDiary
data.description: Electronic diary device used by participants to record daily CDAI patient-reported outcomes including stool frequency, abdominal pain, general well-being, and bowel movement count during Study Period 1.

data.name: Interactive Web-Response System
data.label: IWRS
data.description: Interactive web-response system used for visit registration, randomization or assignment to ISA, and randomization to study intervention.

data.name: Genetics Sample Retention
data.description: A genetics blood sample is collected at or after Visit 2 (Week 0) if country regulations allow, and is stored as a retained sample. The protocol references a dedicated Genetics appendix (Appendix 5), indicating these samples are retained for genetic analysis.

data.name: Exploratory Biomarker Blood Sample Retention
data.description: Exploratory biomarker blood samples are collected and stored at multiple visits throughout the study for future exploratory research purposes.

data.name: Exploratory Biomarker Stool Supernatant Retention
data.description: Stool supernatant samples collected from the same stool sample used for fecal calprotectin testing are stored as exploratory biomarker samples at multiple visits.

data.name: Exploratory Biomarker Colonic Tissue Retention
data.description: Colonic tissue samples obtained from endoscopic biopsy at screening and Week 12 of Study Period 1 are stored as exploratory biomarker samples.
